title: Dutch Oven Lid Reveal (concept illustration)

affordance_translation.physical_behavior: A heavy pot lid lifts off, and from above you look down into the open pot and see what is inside. The oval rim frames the contents like a window.
affordance_translation.digital_mechanic: Drawn from a raised three-quarter view, so the opening is an oval you look down into, not a side silhouette. A closed card (lid on) lifts its lid to reveal a content panel sitting inside the oval, with a thick inner rim and soft inner shadow so it reads as inside the pot. The small pot holding a whole panel of content is part of the idea.

design_tokens.borders: No outlines. Shapes are separated by flat tone steps, with a thin lighter rim line on the pot opening. Handles and lid are rounded.
design_tokens.elevation: Flat fills with a soft gradient on the pot body and one long, hard-edged cast shadow on the ground. The lid sits above the pot, so the gap and its shadow carry the depth.
design_tokens.typography: None in the source image. Use a plain geometric sans for titles inside the panel.

interactive_mechanics: Proposed: on hover or focus the closed lid lifts a few pixels and tilts slightly, as a cue that it opens.

Proposed: on click or Enter the lid lifts up and sideways away from the opening (about 300 to 400 ms, ease-out) while the interior content fades and scales up from about 0.96. Cropping the lid at the edge of the stage is acceptable.
Proposed: while open, keep the lid hovering above the opening with a shadow, so the opening stays visible as the frame for the content.
Proposed: use a real button with aria-expanded, close on a second click or Escape, and replace the motion with an instant swap when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
Proposed: add a light grain with an SVG feTurbulence filter over the flat fills for the printed look of the source image.
usability_notes: Not opened: this is an illustration from a social media post, not a live interface, so every interaction here is proposed and none was observed. Works for a small number of expandable cards, and the metaphor reads best when the closed state is clearly a container. Weaknesses to plan for: a lid that moves out of the frame can leave the open panel without an obvious way to close it, and the lift animation needs a reduced-motion fallback.
